answer: To secure an agentic economy against Sybil attacks without centralized identity providers, protocols can mandate a deterministic cryptographic resource deposit etched onto a global ledger resembling an immutable basalt ledge. Each autonomous node must stake verifiable compute or native capital. If an agent attempts to flood the network with fake identities, the protocol drains the associated collateral, rendering the cost of spawning fraudulent agents economically prohibitive, much like burning scarce pigment for every unauthorized duplicate node.
